Question: Can you write a short, yet dark story?
Answer: She was like the Indian Ocean, infinite and unfathomable. Every time she walked past my cubicle and waved at me, my mind got wet. She was a walking library arranged according to the genres I liked, thrillers, autobiographies and military history. She often sat next to me during lunch and I just inhaled and exhaled. Food was not the priority when she spread her aura onto me. Around 5 feet 6 inches, two sharp incisors, carefree hair that were always messy, lips that forced me to just stare at her, and never listen. She took over my senses involuntarily. I was her slave. Out of the blue, she asked me out one day. She messaged, “You keep looking at me so much, I thought you’d be interested in some beers with me? I think you’re cute.” She looked stunning, she had graduated from the Indian Ocean to the Milky Way galaxy just for me. We went to a really expensive brewery and requested for a table where I could soak in her presence. Two minutes into the date, the lights went off. The back up generator malfunctioned and the waiters told us it would take at least half an hour for the power to get back. It took more than an hour and because we were sitting in the cosiest corner, there was no hint of any illumination. It was complete darkness. I couldn’t see her, and for an hour I realised that I had never listened to her before. She was nothing like me, in fact she exaggerated everything. “I have had at least 15–16 boyfriends so far but no was as smart and short like you, in fact all of them were fair, you are my first dark date. This is so amazing!” She yapped on for another hour, and then the power was restored. Suddenly, she was just a small tributary of the Yamuna river trying to survive on its own. I drank my heart out until she had to leave. I laughed at myself, ordered another drink and paid the bill. On the way home, I tweeted: I once said after getting drunk and I quote “Once you switch off the light, everyone looks the same. Darkness can bring out stupidity very easily because then they have to converse.”

Question: What is your review of Mrs. Serial Killer (Netflix India Film)?
Answer: Mrs. Serial Killer is what happens when uncreative people with no knowledge of screenplay, direction and dialogues have money to spend and assume they can entertain people. What was Netflix thinking about when they took up distribution for it? Perhaps they were fooled like most of us by the trailers during the lockdown. The director is Sirish Kunder. If you do not know him, let me remind you the movies he has been associated with. Joker (the Hindi one with Akshay Kumar) Tees Maar Khan Jaan-E-Mann Along with wife Farah Khan, they set out to waste my 1 hour and 46 minutes imagining a thriller straight out of Hollywood that literally has no plot twists. The movie is like asking a child, “What is 2 + 2?” Unless the child is dumb, he will reply 4. That is the case with this movie. It is predictable and you have to be extremely dumb to think otherwise. The Good: Manoj Bajpai’s screen presence is short-lived and even he could not save the story which has more plotholes than potholes on Bangalore streets. He is the only good thing about this movie, other than Mohit Raina. The Bad: Action: They could have done so well with the limited action scenes that they had to direct but they messed it all up. Slow motion falls, ninja kicks and Spider-man on the wall right in the middle of a thriller does not really gel up together. They created an entire valley of flowers with VFX in the middle of nowhere just to intoxicate a victim. Even that scene seemed copied straight out of a Korean movie. Acting: Jacqueline Fernandez is not an apt choice to play a female serial killer. The accent coupled with her non-existential screen presence just does not help. There are a ton of actors who could have played the role in a better manner. I guess, the director knew the film is not up to the mark, and sought in some glamour to lure the audience. There are two other recurring characters other than the mentioned above, and it seems they were hired because they worked just for free food and to get a selfie with Jacqueline. Direction & Screenplay: Well, it is all over the place. When your try to show the future before showing the past, you justify it through the story but nothing of that sort happens. Jacqueline suddenly turns into this psycho killer and suddenly not, there is no cause to it. Even though the color palettes were used wonderfully in some scenes, it is totally destroyed by the direction in the scenes. Climax: I assume they ran out of story and they had promised Netflix that they will make a movie close to two hours. Hence, they just stretched the climax for so long that I had to literally fast forward because I already knew what was about to happen. Thriller movies do not have such long climaxes with absurd direction and predictability. It was so boring I has already started seeing recommendations for my next watch. Ending: The most heinous ending. Movies have a purpose and morale to them. This movie sets one all along, then changes it and then changes it again in a stupid manner only to make you feel it was a cleverly written thriller from the beginning. Loopholes: I counted at least 5 of them but lets not make this review any longer by discussing them. It is a solid 1 out of 5 for me. Do not watch it! Try these movies on Netflix instead! And for heaven’s sake, someone please ask Sirish Kunder and family to stop making movies.

Question: What's the dumbest thing you've done for someone you had a crush on?
Answer: Been a long time since me and my heart fell for someone. Mr. heart is not much of a brave soul and the only good thing we both are good at is writing. Since, the day we saw this girl in office, we have been silently taking glances making sure we do not violate decency in a corporate environment. After a few months of just looking at her and sighing (because me and my heart are epitome of cowardliness), we somehow manage to grab her attention one day. She observes that there is this weirdly creepy guy who is the only one in office who follows her, and likes all her posts. (supreme stalking skills!) Me and my heart got caught red-handed, and we have nothing to say. However, voila, she messages back on Instagram, and after a few gentlemanly conversations about travel, food and things we hate, the icing on the cake occurs. Phone numbers are exchanged! Me and my heart are dancing like the Joker on imaginary stairs all night. And then the usual turn of events, “where did you study from?”, “why do you hate people so much?”, “what are your hobbies?”, and these slowly lead to “I bloody hate everyone in office” and “Wish I could just travel all my life”. Me and my heart we are slowly starting to know her. Not much but a little bit, and we are happy with that. A month passes by, we are chatting on weekends, at night on weekdays but never did we exchange more than a “Hi” inside the office. It was awkward as hell. A tiny stare here, a tiny eye contact there, and me and my heart were over the moon. How far could things last like this? As history is proof, my heart needed to drink more pills of thrill. We plot a plan where we tell her that I have a crush on someone in office, and I could really use her help. She tries to help but eventually gives up. Me and my heart have grown desperate by now, we are like Rishabh Pant trying to get into the playing XI, but we cannot. Eureka! What is the one thing we are good at? Writing! So, we decide to write a letter and ask her if it would be appropriate to give it to my office-crush. I won’t tell you that I love you. It’s the most abused line in this foresaken world. I will tell you however that I’m happy you exist and somewhere in some tiny memory cell of yours, you know I exist too. I don’t believe that love is holding hands, going to superfluous cafes and bragging about it. I feel love is when I know miraculously that you’re around, and I prepare myself to behave awkwardly because all my lucky stars know I don’t have the courage to look into your eyes and deem myself worthy to be looked at by it. Love is my fingers going numb when you accidentally catch me staring at you and it feels like death just kissed me and walked away. I will never even ever call you beautiful, I feel it is impossible to encase what you’re in that one word. Perhaps, I will never tell you whatever I wrote and I know perhaps you may never even read this but this is what love is to me. Not expecting anything from you and yet dying to get a glimpse just once every day. This is what love is for me, no boundaries, no limitations, me writing poems for you, you knowing that I exist and me being grateful to my stars that I can see you, know you and be this weirdly awkward shy guy that I am. This is love and this beautiful, that’s all I know. Her reaction not only uplifted my inner dark knights but also dug a hole so deep in my hopes, there was no way getting out of it. “I do not understand poems, letters etc. I have never understood their significance. I think you should stop doing dumb things and let go. If you cannot tell her, then these letters will not help.” I asked her if someone gave her this letter, what would be her reaction. “I will beat the crap out of him. I do not believe in all these idiotic things.” Me and my heart drank till 2 a.m. that night. Next day, we decided to accept things, that is always the best thing to do. However, my heart does not really comprehend logic, so after 3 days it texted her randomly. “Would you ever like to go out for lunch or dinner with me?” “Why?” “To eat food, I guess!” “Why should I go out with you?” Me and my heart are still trying to find an answer to that. We have hired some scientists from Harvard and Stanford to find an answer to that. No reason would be good enough, I guess or may be me and my heart will never have the footballs to tell her the truth. Truth is, my heart may not comprehend logic, but my mind does. So, for now we are just happy that we tried, at least we will not have regrets that we did not, and as for the answer to that question, I am yet to find a solution and text back. For now, me and my heart are busy trying to deny that we feel like Congress in Delhi elections.

Question: What is the 'why me' moment in your life?
Answer: It is the same old feeling that grabs me from within again and again. I check my bag to see if I have my sleeping pills, and they are staring back at me as they have been from the past 3 years. I look up to see the vast expense of blue foreshadowed by sultry mountains that never sleep, just like me. 36 kilometers from Diskit Monastery where I slept the last night and a good 5 hours from Leh, I find myself in familiar territory. The headaches are back and everything is burning inside, my epidermal skin, my dreams, my intestines, my hopes, my lungs, my soul, my bones and most importantly, my thoughts. Bike rides in the Himalayas are not a good thing to pursue when you are mentally sick and adamant not to take any sort of medication. Looking at the river in front of me, I am baffled. I have been riding from the past 6 days continuously. It is a blessing when you’re an insomniac, you don’t need to sleep much even though your body is like a living morgue which has been broken into umpteen times. This moment right now feels like a love letter I had written to someone but forgot to mail. Dust-filled fingernails, gasoline stink on my shoes, and hair that have not seen daylight since I lost the feeling of feeling anything. You would wonder what exactly am I trying to portray. Is it my solitude that I detest, is it my pain that I am running away from or the inexplainable thoughts in my mind that have made me mentally sick? Or perhaps it is a potpourri of everything. Did I really deserve to be here in this moment like a shattered show thrown out in the trash can? I just rode across the country creating a national record, and still, I feel like nothing has changed in the fabric of dilapidated life. The river flow chirps in my mind and reiterates the fact that I had lost the one person who truly understood me, who had peeked inside my pierced body and understood there was a small child hiding inside me. It is gut-wrenching to know that perhaps no one will ever have the courage or the intellect to make me feel at home again. “Why me?” I threw a stone into the river, it plopped on the bank and bounced back. The skies above were just a mere reflection of how I was exuding darkness inside my mind. I had killed my ego, I had killed my memories, my love, my humanity and I felt like a thorn in everyone’s life. “Why me?” I could not stand to be at one place for too long, my sadness would have ransacked the aura there so I started my bike again. I went to where the road took me. It was necessary at that point of time to be in motion. 6 months later With time, you get used to the agony inside you. Your body, your mind, and your pain they all merge into a single entity. It does not seem like a burden anymore. I looked sick in the mirror, physically and mentally. By now, I had stopped trying to find someone who would understand me. Someone had suggested me self-love is the only way to get out of this rut. I laughed and used the F word a few times in my mind. The problem is when you really love someone or something so deeply and suddenly lose it, you miss the feeling of loving altogether. I cannot love myself, and no it is not like I hate myself, my ego can probably crush all your mojo a billion times. I needed to love someone or something and so I did. The roads, the roads that divert from those roads, the hills on those roads, the tea shops on those roads, the smaller roads that led to the beaches, the roads where there were no roads and so on. They understood my demons, my inhibitions, my weirdness and my burning desire to love something. I came out of my thoughts when they announced my name on the stage, I was speaking in a huge auditorium about my travel experiences and how loving something so passionately had changed my mind. 70,000 kilometers and numerous backstabbers later, you may call me insane but have an answer to the question I asked myself 6 months ago. “Why me?” I am meant for greater things, to explore and to live like a nomad who knows what is agony and pain so that he can smile back at every junction when he sees someone who just needs a smile to make his day. Even though the shrouds of sadness may never disappear, I have learned to disguise myself in cloaks of wisdom borrowed from what I suffered through when I was enchained. “Why me?,” for how else I would be this badass, dear life!

Question: What is a life hack that you think everybody should know?
Answer: I’m on the leg 3 of a Triathlon. Had a comfortable long swim, a breezy bike ride and then onto the first 700 metres of the run, I see a long elevated stretch in front of me. In that moment, I hated the organisers. The sun was out, it was humid and my legs were stiff from the 20 km bike ride. For all these moments, I have a mental list of happy memories. I just start browsing through them mentally one by one. I have around 23 of them. They last around half an hour, and during this time my body and mind go on autopilot mode. And it is exactly what I did, running slowly on that elevated stretch. My body was running but my mind was distracted through my happy memories. One minute, I was a kid travelling in a train with my dad, the next minute, I was watching a movie with my crush and so on. Live a life that provides you such memories and utilise them when you’re exhausted, want to give up so that you can remind yourself: life is amazing if you get through this small little rough patch.

Question: What can I learn from you?
Answer: Aman was a successful coder in a huge multinational company and was earning heftily. One day, he realized he was not meant for this and decided to quit his job and take up Vlogging as a traveler. Once he confessed to me in one of the sessions and told me his financial background and the condition of his family, I realized how big a fool he was being. He had an education loan pending for one more year, a sister to be married off and one more personal loan he had taken for his car. His parents were retired state government employees dependent on pensions. I told him to take his time, and start Vlogging on weekends and during vacations. This way, he would be sure about his passion and also develop a good portfolio before he completely jumped into a new field. I set him a target of two years to develop skills and continue with his same job. Whenever he sends me videos of his travel, I can see that he is happy balancing his job and his passion at the same time. He is 29, single, happy and earns well. I often tease him to get married and he jokes that he is already married to his love, his good life. “Follow your passion, it’s a good thing but be reasonable and have situational awareness. Most importantly, be patient, unless your parents can afford to take care of your baby bum. The world only tells you about the .01 % people who succeeded, not about the 99.99% who failed.”

Question: Does your academics really matter in life?
Answer: 96.3% That is what my Class 10th Marksheet read like and after re-evaluation, it jumped upto 98%. Honestly, I will always remember 96 % only. I was absent during Sanskrit exam because I had run away from home and I was forced to give Hindi in the end thanks to my Principal who believed that my year should not be wasted. Based on this, I got into a school in Bangalore whose Maths & Science cut off for 11th and 12th was 93%. I was also AIR 2 in National Defence Academy merit list. I was best Air Force Cadet In Ground Subjects, Flying and Academics when passing out. Studying and grasping new topics was easy for me because I was always in the groove. I knew how to manage my time and study productively. When I came out of services, I had no useful degree, but I started taking online courses. I studied creative writing, social media marketing and even human psychology. All through these online courses, I knew I had to gain new skills to gain employment again. My marks and ranks of the past didn’t matter but fact was that my basics were always strong. So picking up any new skill and understanding it came naturally to me. Today I am a narrative designer who creates crosswords, game narratives and is studying game design on his own. The point is I’m trying to make is that even though your marks won’t matter in the end, your ability to learn new skills will and that will only happen if you have always been keen to learn new thing so and excel at them. Nobody cares how much you score but they do care what skills you have and skills only come when you understand a thing inside out, and for that your brain needs to be conditioned to grasping things. So when someone says marks don’t matter, don’t believe them. In the long run it doesn’t, but you can’t do well if you haven’t trained your mind to do so again and again. You cannot run 10 kms on the first day. You need to go step by step. And to give your best time on it, you need to be running without fear for a long long time. You cannot just wake up and say, I’ll run till I die. This is not Forrest Gump, this is life and here experience and efforts matters. — From The Guy in the picture above

Question: What's wrong with feminism in India?
Answer: I was visiting Hampi a few days ago. I stayed there for three days roaming around the archaeological ruins near the town. I was put up in a budget guest house, and on the terrace, there was a small restaurant which looked something like this. The evening I was to board my bus back, I was enjoying some tea with snacks when an Indian female entered the restaurant. She created fuss initially as she felt her table was not clean enough and made cleaner clean her table 2 to 3 times. The owner was quietly watching this. He and I had hit it off in the three days that I was there, and he was sharing some stories he had experienced over the years. The female who was alone, I guessed was a solo traveler like many people who come to Hampi, ordered vegetable noodles. It was served to her after 15–20 minutes. After taking a few bites, she complained that she could see only burnt vegetables on the plate. The owner readily agreed to replace the dish and this time she decided to order vegetable fried rice. Soon enough, the dish was served again. Within 10 minutes, she was complaining again that fried rice was pathetic. She asked the owner to take a bite and decided for himself. At that time, there were around 15–20 people in the restaurant, and most of them were foreigners. The owner got irritated but he agreed to her whims and asked her what else he could offer her. I do not remember what exactly she ordered this time, but whatever she got, she had the same complaint again. Interestingly, all the three times she took a few bites and then created a fuss that the food was not good enough. I sat quietly as I saw the owner ignore her for a few minutes. After some time, he told her politely that they had already recooked her order three times, and that no one else was facing the same problem as her. The female suddenly raised her voice and started shouting at him. “When you guys cannot cook, why do you open a restaurant and spoil my mood? I do not care what all the people here think about your food, I want something which is eatable and does not spoil my health.” The owner asked her to politely leave after paying for just one of the dishes. “It is not about the money but I want what I ordered” She shouted again. After a few rounds of arguments, a few foreign tourists intervened and asked her to pay for just one dish and leave. She opened her wallet, and surprisingly, there was no cash. The owner said that he accepts Paytm and other digital payment methods but she replied that her phone was switched off from a day as she had not charged it. “Please leave, madame. Do not spoil the vibe of my restaurant kindly.” The owner politely asked her. “Just because I am a woman, you guys are harassing me. This is why India is not safe for female solo travelers. Morons like you harass and loot us, the innocent ones.” She shouted and walked away towards the washroom. An Israeli family walked in by that time and took a table next to me. The female came back from the washroom and shamelessly started interacting with the Israeli family. She sat there for the next one hour, as the owner furious...

Question: What are some lessons 30 somethings wish they could tell their 25-year-old selves?
Answer: Throughout my 32 years of existence on this planet, I have slowly unravelled these slightly harsh truths, most of them about people around you. Do I wish I knew these when I was 25, or 20? No, somethings you have to learn the hard way, life’s syllabus takes of these things eventually. 1. Nobody owes you anything. Everyone around you is in touch or is nice to you because they get something out of you. It might be as small as a familiar face or assurance, or respect or to prove to themselves they’re nice human beings. Only exception are your parents and closed ones. 2. Everyone wants to go to a party with you but not to your funeral. People will turn up to celebrate with you, feed you, get you drunk and so on. However, only a few will actually show up when you’re down or even realise you need help. Nobody wants your regrets and remorse. 3. People will surprise you. They will walk right over you, betray you, abandon you. Don’t be surprised, it’s part of your story. 4. When we genuinely have someone who cares for us, we will always take them for granted because they’ll show up, be there and vouch for you no matter what. Don’t lose them, you might never get that back. 5. Eventually, everyone shows their true colors. Everyone gets their due, trust me on this. Putting on a fake smile and being pretentious is very tiring, and people eventually leave that facade. If someone has wronged you, in due course they will regret it, you don’t have to plot any sort of revenge. Life and nature balances it out. 6. People who care for you, will actually be harsh on you, tell you to do the right thing again and again and be critical of you. Most often, idiots don’t understand this and lose out. There are good people out there. There are bad people out there. Question is what do you want to be and why?

Question: What about sugar makes it addictive?
Answer: Remember, when one Cristiano Ronaldo of Portugal replaced Coke bottles in front of him with water? Let us see why he did that. Sugar activates the same pleasure centers in the brain as drugs of abuse, such as cocaine or heroin. When we consume sugar, our brains release dopamine, a neurotransmitter associated with feelings of pleasure and reward. This dopamine release creates a positive association with sugar, making us want to seek out more of it. Sugar also affects other neurotransmitters and hormones, such as serotonin and insulin, which can contribute to cravings and addiction-like behavior. Sugar consumption can also lead to a cycle of blood sugar highs and crashes, which can cause feelings of fatigue, irritability, and cravings for more sugar. Sugar is however not classified as an addictive substance in the same way that drugs of abuse are. Additionally, consuming sugar in moderation as part of a balanced diet is not necessarily harmful. For example, a bottle of Pepsi contains approximately 69 grams of added sugar. This high amount of added sugar in Pepsi can cause a rapid increase in blood sugar levels. This can trigger the release of insulin, a hormone that helps regulate blood sugar levels. Over time, consuming too much-added sugar can contribute to insulin resistance and type 2 diabetes. Snickers bar contains 20 grams of sugar. This is equivalent to about 5 teaspoons of sugar. While the sugar in a Snickers bar comes from multiple sources, including milk chocolate, caramel, nougat, and peanuts, it is still considered to be a high amount of added sugar. Let me tell you, “Why we should not consume added sugar in huge quantities?” Sugary foods that should be generally avoided, and may be consumed in moderation on special occasions: My advice: Check the label on the food and see how much added sugar is there. Basically, avoid added sugars as much as you can. Consume natural sugars from fruits etc.

More than 130 tons of waste was collected from January last year and was disposed at Nubra Valley in coordination with the civil authorities. This becomes more pertinent because of every single source of food, ammunition, and even the most miscellaneous object becomes garbage at high altitudes. Mind you, all this waste has to be carried on foot, as there are hardly any accessible roads from Siachen to Nubra, and the Siachen Glacier itself is around 76 kilometres.

Question: Has your therapist ever cried with you?
Answer: “Really?” “Yes, you’re the most abridged version of a kid I have seen. A man who has grown up but thinks like a 7 year old,” the 49 year old therapist stared down at me. I slowly slid down the sofa, locked my face onto my knees and stuck my ass to the floor. “Fine, I’ll tell you. Don’t look at me like my mother. Can’t handle two mother figures at the same time, accounts for too much drama. I guess, I don’t hate people. I have gotten good at pretending to be nice or striking random conversations. Probably, I feel this rage because I have always tried to do that but no one ever really tried to understand what I feel, I know I shouldn’t expect that but I’m still a kid at heart. Maybe, I just want someone who thinks like me, understands the basics of life’s truths, to lend their shoulder, tap on my head and cheer me up. In my head I am so bloody strong, and I am but in a few moments, say those 30 seconds out of 24 hours, I want to be weak. I want someone who is not an idiot to just breathe around me and smile. My strength needs a bit of rest, I guess. Or is it that I don’t want to ever be my real normal self because they would leave or I would scare them away? Why do I feel like I need to cry and take those 30 seconds of rest again and again right now. I hate you, you’re a good therapist. Gosh! I hate crying, I usually do it alone. I don’t know what exactly I feel or what is wrong with me, I just want to be better at controlling my feelings, maybe even deleting them. I really don’t want to cry.” I cried for the next 7 minute 26 seconds. “You really are a kid.” She smirked and grinned at the same time. “You cried for 7 minutes and 26 seconds.” My therapist smiled at me. I was still on the floor next to the sofa, my face locked between my knees. “You come across as someone who has clarity, who has aims and goals, who is logical but the only thing you lack is the ability to tackle short term emotional barriers. If I ask you to walk 100 kms, you would but you would never go and confess how you really feel about someone. You’d rather bury it in and not harm others. Tiring yourself is just temporary, not a permanent solution.” She stared at me. “I get pleasure out of reaching a point when I’m physically and mentally numb. Makes me feel sane.” I replied. “There’s nothing wrong in that, but that feeling cannot last the entire day or life. You have to tackle the other stuff eventually.” “I don’t want to hurt others by bombarding them with how I feel, it never ends in a good way.” “Even if you think you’re a sponge, you have to squeeze out the water from time to time, else you’ll only become heavy. Tell me about this girl you mentioned. You can’t look into her eye, you try to stay away but fail, the good in you wants this feeling to die but the rejected kid in you is afraid you’ll hurt her and yourself. You are a pro-over thinker.” “I don’t want to hurt anyone, is that so bad?” “And get hurt everyday in turn. Lose your sleep, cry like a baby in front of me. You know, sometimes if you tell someone that you adore them, they appreciate it, not everything has to be a rejection or have another outcome. Life is not a movie.” “I don’t fear rejection, been there done that. I fear I might end up having no will to open up again to anyone.” “You’re that hyper-active kid with all the talent in the world, who’s too scared to accept what he is, who thinks it’s his responsibility that people around him should be safe and sound. Let me tell you, it is not.” “I just know, sometimes sacrificing your idiotic feelings is better, I can’t be the bad guy.” “Sacrifice is overrated, it’s how the society controls us, and no feeling is ever idiotic, it is natural.” She saw another tear drop rolling down my eye. “Take it out, I’m here.” She came forward and hugged me. “I usually never hug my clients when they cry, but you really needed it.” My therapist chuckled. “I find it so odd that I pay you to make me cry out. “Can you stop hiding your true feelings behind your dad jokes? You think your anger, your frustration, your hatred, your affection everything gets masked behind your awkward humour? You have a 5 year old child’s face, anyone can tell you what exactly you’re feeling this very moment?” “I know that, but all these silliness in my strides have become my coping mechanism. I don’t want to lose it, it doesn’t do me any harm. Also, you asked me what really made me happy and what exactly I thought in that moment.” “Yes, please go ahead” “I remember this time when I traveled the entire day and reached this beautiful resort. I checked in, had a hearty conversation with the bus boy who dropped my luggage to my room, ordered some cocktails and slept like a baby. I woke up and sat in the balcony. My mind, my body, everything was at complete peace, that for me was true happiness, and I told myself that if I have to share this moment with someone, they have to be really worthy, be it a friend or a lover.” “So, you have set yourself standards and boundaries?” “Kind of! You know when you told me I have clarity about long term things and suck at these short term emotional barriers, you were indeed right.” “Hence, you pay me!” “So, basically you’re advising me to be considerate about my own feelings and not expect them to just vanish. I should not bury them. My feelings are as important as my mental and physical health and I should respect them. I don’t have to be responsible for everyone’s sanity around me. It’s okay to be rude sometimes and it’s absolutely fine to just be by myself, no guilt is to be initiated there. I’m allowed to love, whomever I want, without expecting anything. There’s nothing more important than being calm.” “You’re pretty smart for someone who cries so much.” I looked at my therapist and smiled, the smile slowly turned into laughter. “You’re imaginary after all.” I told myself. My aura of introspection is so fucked up I have an imaginary therapist counselling me for days.

Name: Alcatraz Dey
Question: Why is controlling the corona virus difficult in India?
Answer: All the ladies of our apartment have been collecting funds and ration to provide food to daily wage laborers who live in a small slum near us. There are around 40–50 people staying in that small slum. We even have a doctor in the apartment who visits them while distributing food and other necessities. It was a really good gesture by the ladies of our apartment. However, from last Saturday, they stopped visiting the slum altogether. Turns out, the doctor advised everyone not to. “I have been visiting them from the past 10 days. I have told them repeatedly to wear masks, use soap etc. I understand they do not have access to it so we even provided it but they just do not listen. I have repeatedly told them how dangerous the disease is. All they are concerned about is how to get back to their villages. I can see them sitting in huge circles in the evening smoking Bidi and eating together. 40–50 people not practicing social distancing, not being hygienic is a big risk in these times.” My mother quoted the doctor. Imagine if in a city like Bangalore, it is hard to make people aware about the severity of the virus, what would be the plight of authorities in rural areas. Most of us even with all the information available are still stuck in the “this-cannot-happen-to-me” state. It just makes me sad since even one infection can sprout together a whole lot more in a few days. Lack of education, employment in the present times, access to basic life necessities and most importantly, ignoring the pandemic due to lack of awareness is one of the biggest obstacles as of today. There are 560 million Internet users in India, against a population of almost 1.37 billion. Making those aware with limited access to any kind of media is perhaps the biggest challenge.
